# Metrics reference

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen-reference.py from a running node's /metrics and the source. Do not edit by hand; CI fails when a metric is missing from it. -->

Every node serves Prometheus metrics at `http://127.0.0.1:7776/metrics` — loopback only
unless `[http] addr` says otherwise ([configuration](config.md#http)) — with no exporter
to install. `/healthz` on the same port answers `200` with a JSON summary while the node
is healthy and `503` with the reasons in `"problems"` when it is not.

```console
$ curl -s localhost:7776/metrics | grep meshware_jobs_running
$ curl -s localhost:7776/healthz
```

Every family is **this node's own view**: scrape every node, and aggregate in Prometheus.

| Metric | Type | Labels | What it measures |
|---|---|---|---|
| `meshware_uptime_seconds` | gauge | — | Seconds since this node started. |
| `meshware_draining` | gauge | — | 1 while the node is draining. |
| `meshware_cgroup_enforcing` | gauge | — | 1 when declared cpu/memory limits are enforced per job (cgroups v2 delegation). |
| `meshware_members_total` | gauge | — | Machines in the mesh (not left, not revoked). |
| `meshware_members_alive` | gauge | — | Machines currently observed alive (same census as members_total). |
| `meshware_executor_slots` | gauge | — | Concurrent executor slots on this node. |
| `meshware_executor_slots_available` | gauge | — | Executor slots this node will start work in right now, after quiet hours. |
| `meshware_jobs_running` | gauge | — | Jobs executing on this node right now. |
| `meshware_jobs_queued` | gauge | — | Jobs waiting in this node's pending queue. |
| `meshware_bundles_known` | gauge | — | Bundles known to the mesh. |
| `meshware_bundles_local` | gauge | — | Bundles held complete on this node. |
| `meshware_services` | gauge | — | Live services. |
| `meshware_secrets` | gauge | — | Live secrets. |
| `meshware_git_sources` | gauge | — | Registered Git sources. |
| `meshware_clock_skew_ahead_seconds` | gauge | — | How far the freshest peer clock runs ahead of local time. |
| `meshware_relay_enabled` | gauge | — | 1 while this node relays for NATed members. |
| `meshware_relay_clients` | gauge | — | NATed members registered with this relay. |
| `meshware_relay_paths_open` | gauge | — | Relayed paths currently open through this node. |
| `meshware_sessions_live` | gauge | — | Live sessions this node is party to (hosted and initiated). |
| `meshware_sessions_hosted` | gauge | — | Live sessions this node is hosting — the ones a drain closes. |
| `meshware_jobs_accepted_total` | counter | — | Jobs this node took on, whether they ran at once or queued. |
| `meshware_jobs_started_total` | counter | — | Jobs this node promoted out of its queue into a slot. |
| `meshware_jobs_refused_total` | counter | — | Submissions this node refused at admission — full, out of capacity, or without the device asked for. The number a node is sized by. |
| `meshware_relay_frames_total` | counter | — | Frames switched by this relay. |
| `meshware_relay_bytes_total` | counter | — | Bytes switched by this relay. |
| `meshware_relay_dropped_total` | counter | — | Frames this relay dropped (queue full / no route / oversize). |
| `meshware_relayed_frames_sent_total` | counter | — | Own traffic sent through relays (relay data plane). |
| `meshware_relayed_frames_recv_total` | counter | — | Own traffic received through relays (relay data plane). |
| `meshware_sessions_opened_total` | counter | — | Sessions admitted since this node started. |
| `meshware_sessions_refused_total` | counter | — | Sessions refused by the per-peer cap ([sessions] max_per_peer). |
| `meshware_session_bytes_total` | counter | — | Bytes moved through sessions in both directions. |
| `meshware_jobs_finished_total` | counter | `state` | Terminal jobs executed by this node, by state, counted as they finished. |
| `meshware_jobs_recorded` | gauge | `state` | Terminal job records this node still holds, by state. Falls as retention prunes; see meshware_jobs_finished_total for the count. |
| `meshware_job_queue_wait_seconds` | histogram | — | Time a job spent between arriving here and starting, in seconds. |
| `meshware_job_duration_seconds` | histogram | — | Time a job spent running on this node, in seconds. |
| `meshware_ipc_seconds` | histogram | — | Time from a local request arriving to this node answering it, in seconds. The meter for whether the daemon is responsive, which every other gauge here assumes. |
| `meshware_disk_free_bytes` | gauge | — | Free space on the volume holding this node's data directory. |
| `meshware_disk_total_bytes` | gauge | — | Size of the volume holding this node's data directory. |
| `meshware_disk_critical` | gauge | — | 1 when this node is below its free-space floor and refusing new content. |
| `meshware_oplog_store_bytes` | gauge | — | Op-log store size on disk, read directly rather than from the census cache — so it is present on the first scrape after a restart. |
| `process_resident_memory_bytes` | gauge | — | Resident set size of the meshnode process. |
| `process_open_fds` | gauge | — | Open file descriptors held by the meshnode process. A node that leaks these stops accepting connections long before it stops running. |
| `meshware_members_unreachable` | gauge | — | Members this node cannot currently reach — the same census meshware_members_alive comes from, counted the other way. |
| `meshware_dispatch_seconds` | histogram | — | Time from a submission arriving to a node accepting it, in seconds — selector, feasibility, grants, ranking, cache lookup and the round trip, spills included. Stops at accepted: what follows is the workload's time, not the scheduler's. |
| `meshware_dispatch_failures_total` | counter | `reason` | Submissions an executor did not take, by why. |
| `meshware_dispatch_spills_total` | counter | — | Submissions that moved on to another candidate. |
| `meshware_group_runs_started_total` | counter | `kind` | Fan-out, parallel and gang runs this node began owning, by kind. |
| `meshware_group_runs_finished_total` | counter | `kind`, `outcome` | Group runs this node owned that ended, by kind and how they ended. `halted` stopped early on purpose; `failed` ran and lost a target. |
| `meshware_group_subjobs_total` | counter | `kind`, `outcome` | Sub-jobs of the group runs this node owned, by kind and outcome. `skipped` never became a job on any node, so nothing else in the mesh records it. |
| `meshware_group_run_seconds` | histogram | `kind` | Wall time a group run this node owned took, from the plan being replicated to the last target reporting. |
| `meshware_peer_alive` | gauge | `name`, `peer` | 1 while this node currently observes a peer as alive. One sample per member of the mesh, from this node's point of view: a peer that is up everywhere else and 0 here is a partition, and no fleet-wide gauge can show that. |
| `meshware_ops_parked` | gauge | — | Ops the last apply pass could not take, because whatever would authorize them has not arrived. A gauge: a parked op is re-fetched on the next sync rather than consumed, so what matters is the standing backlog. Zero on a healthy node. |
| `meshware_refusals_total` | counter | `limit` | Requests and ops a limit turned away, by which limit. `op_rate` is the per-entity op-rate guard; `enrol_*` and `login_*` are the two doors open to any key holder, limited per source and overall. |
| `meshware_op_rate_pauses_total` | counter | — | Times the op-rate guard put an entity in a pause after repeated refusals. Each one is a workload that kept pushing after being told to stop. |
| `meshware_build_info` | gauge | `protocol`, `version` | Build metadata. |

## Emitted only when there is something to report

A node leaves these out entirely, rather than reporting a zero, until the condition
holds — a saturated GPU that reads as idle is worse than no series at all.

| Metric | When | Labels | What it measures |
|---|---|---|---|
| `meshware_gpu_held` | on a node with accelerators whose telemetry has arrived | `index`, `model`, `vendor` | 1 when a job or gang holds a lease on this device. Different from utilisation: a held card at 0% is not a free card. |
| `meshware_gpu_memory_free_mb` | on a node with accelerators whose telemetry has arrived | `index`, `model`, `vendor` | Free device memory in MB. |
| `meshware_gpu_temperature_celsius` | on a node with accelerators whose telemetry has arrived | `index`, `model`, `vendor` | Device temperature. |
| `meshware_gpu_throttled` | on a node with accelerators whose telemetry has arrived | `index`, `model`, `vendor` | 1 when the driver reports the device throttled — the reason a card at 100% is doing less work than yesterday. |
| `meshware_gpu_utilisation_pct` | on a node with accelerators whose telemetry has arrived | `index`, `model`, `vendor` | Accelerator utilisation, 0-100, as the driver reports it. |
| `meshware_oplog_bytes` | once the op-log census has been taken (shortly after start) | — | Op-log size on disk. |
| `meshware_oplog_ops_total` | once the op-log census has been taken (shortly after start) | `kind` | Ops in the log, by entity kind. |
| `meshware_oplog_surviving_bytes_per_day` | once the op-log census has been taken (shortly after start) | — | Estimated bytes of permanent op-log growth per day — what a year of this mesh costs. |
| `meshware_oplog_surviving_ops` | once the op-log census has been taken (shortly after start) | `kind` | Ops no compaction pass can ever drop, by entity kind. |
| `meshware_peer_sync_age_seconds` | once this node has peers | `name`, `peer` | How long ago a peer last asked this node for ops. Rising on a peer that is alive is the shape of a stuck sync. |
| `meshware_peer_sync_behind_ops` | once this node has peers | `name`, `peer` | Ops of this node's log a peer had not received when it last asked. Absent for a peer that has not asked. |
| `meshware_sink_dropped_total` | on the node exporting for at least one sink | `sink` | Batches dropped because the spool filled. These rows are gone. |
| `meshware_sink_lag_seconds` | on the node exporting for at least one sink | `sink` | How far behind a sink is, in the data's own clock. |
| `meshware_sink_sent_total` | on the node exporting for at least one sink | `sink` | Rows a sink has accepted. |
| `meshware_sink_spooled_bytes` | on the node exporting for at least one sink | `sink` | Bytes a sink is holding because its destination refused them. |
